correctness.rationale: Translation fits exactly when each projected span fits; six strip inequalities form two regular hexagons rotated 30 degrees. Exact clipping geometry gives the 12-to-6 vertex transition, cyclic vertex radius and area. Polar area equals pi times the squared-scale mean. On circles below the outermost vertex radius the forbidden intervals for active facets are pairwise disjoint, giving the exact all-threshold survival law. Normalized formulas are monotone in aspect ratio with strict equality cases. The independent checker reconstructed 12 halfplane intersections and compared 48 survival values; these numerical tests corroborate the complete analytic proof rather than certify infinite statements.

value.rationale: Orientation-dependent maximal containment scale is the fundamental continuous invariant studied by similarity-containment theory. The new result supplies a complete law for a natural source/target family, sharp width-ratio type transitions and an exact second moment with a uniquely square fixed-area optimizer. It also compares this new average-case theorem with the credited classical best-single-orientation rectangle aspect ratio \(2/\sqrt3\). It is neither a recomputed classical endpoint nor a tailored finite test.
